title: Incident (data/incidents/<id>.json), v1
description: One persistent record per real-world incident (outage, breach, vulnerability campaign). Daily stories and weekly themes point at it with incidentId instead of repeating its status. File name must be <id>.json. Additional properties are allowed.

provider.description: Affected provider, vendor, operator or project (for example "Microsoft", "Equinor", "OpenJDK").

category.description: Optional topic category (same vocabulary as story categories); drives the accent colour.

summary.description: Current one-paragraph state of the incident. Rewrite it as facts change; the history keeps the earlier states.

status.description: Current status. investigating: scope or cause unknown. identified: cause or scope known, fix not yet in place. monitoring: mitigation applied, watching for recurrence or full recovery. resolved: service restored or vulnerability patched (resolvedDate required).

discoveredDate.description: Date the incident was first reported or noticed (Pacific).

occurredDate.description: Date the incident actually began or the flaw was introduced, when known and different from discovery.

resolvedDate.description: Date service was restored or the immediate threat ended. Set only when status is resolved.

fixDate.description: Date a permanent fix (patch, architectural change, rollback policy) shipped. May be later than resolvedDate.

fix.description: What the permanent fix is. Distinct from rootCause and from any temporary mitigation.

status.description: unknown: not disclosed. suspected: researcher or press inference. confirmed: stated by the affected party or a postmortem.

postmortems.description: Official or independent postmortems, added whenever they are published.

sources.description: Primary and best secondary sources for the incident as a whole.

history.description: Chronological, append-only timeline (oldest first). Each entry records what became known on that date.

status.description: Status as of this entry. The last entry that sets one must equal the incident status.
